translation_notes: The predicate is an f-string hole spliced INSIDE the SPARQL angle brackets (`<{EX_P}>`), i.e. textual query assembly; in ldpy this becomes {URIRef(EX_P)} as the whole predicate term (term-position interpolation, an initBindings entry) inside s{ SELECT ?s ?o WHERE { ?s {URIRef(EX_P)} ?o } ORDER BY ?s } -- no query text is concatenated, and EX_P (a bare str) is wrapped in URIRef(...) because a plain string interpolated in term position would coerce to a Literal, not an IRI.

Also translated the two isolated g.add() calls (add_isolated, same region) to a single +{ } with two `.`-separated triples: most-specific construction per INSTRUCTIONS_403 SS2, not left as raw rdflib .add().
ordered=True in the driver because the region's own query specifies ORDER BY ?s.

Correction du 2026-10-30 : la traduction renvoyait `return s{ ... }`, un PreparedQuery paresseux, là où l'original renvoie un rdflib Result (g.query) ; Values.execute exige `isinstance(data, Result)` (values.py:67) et lit data.vars et data.bindings. Écrit `s{ ... }(g).execute()`. Le pilote, qui matérialise tout itérable, ne voyait pas la différence ; il observe maintenant le type, vars, bindings et les lignes.

repair.driver: driver.py réécrit à la main (run_pair matérialise tout itérable, donc un PreparedQuery et un Result s'y confondent) : chaque côté est appelé deux fois, et le pilote compare isinstance(r, Result), r.type, r.vars, r.bindings et les lignes itérées, dans l'ordre (ORDER BY ?s), comme Values.execute les lit ; il constate aussi que l'original rend un Result.
mutants_killed: retrait de `(g).execute()` (l'ancienne traduction : PreparedQuery, is_rdflib_Result True vs False, vars et bindings absents)
repair.remaining: Le mutant qui remplace le prédicat `{URIRef(EX_P)}` par une variable reste vert, équivalent : la région construit elle-même un graphe qui n'a qu'un prédicat, rien ne peut le distinguer.

optimization_notes: optimized.py: the two `g.add` calls become one `g += [...]`; the query stays the original f-string, since the function must return an rdflib Result.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: the graph is one `g{ }` with `f<{EX_A}>`/`f<{EX_P}>` (absolute IRIs, no @base, so the same as URIRef), and the query is `s{ ... ?s f<{EX_P}> ?o ... }(g).execute()`, an initial binding instead of string pasting. Nesting the `g{ }` into the s{ } call would save three more tokens; it was not done, to keep the two statements of optimized.py. No exception to the symmetry.
header_optimization_notes: Python: BNode goes from the rdflib import.
LD Python: the whole rdflib import goes (g{ }, the literals and f<…> name no rdflib class); the three EX_* constants stay.
